items.t: and divide by 3. The resulting number is eighteen (18), with a remainder of one (1).
According to the method known until now, when the threefold wafq has a remainder of one (1), one (1) extra is added to the seventh (7) cell; when the remainder is two (2), one (1)
extra is added to the fourth (4) cell, and the wafq is made in this way. We made the wafq of the number sixty-seven (67). This is its form:

As can be seen, we made this by adding the remainder of one (1) as an extra to the seventh (7) cell. The left diagonal came out one (1) short. For this reason this wafq is not equal, and being wrong, it is not used.
Chapter 3 (al-bāb al-thālith): On the astrological judgements (aḥkām) governing the twenty-eight lunar mansions of the celestial sphere [24]

Here we set out a table of great utility, from which one may know, for the new crescent of every month, in which mansion it stands — and more besides. The method of the two is that you should determine the end of the Arab [lunar] month, for the sun and the moon are then in one mansion. Then determine, of that day, whether it falls in the first third of the Rūmī [solar] month, or the second, or the third, or in the first half or the second half. Then enter with the first day of the Arab month beneath that third or that half, and look to the mansion in which the crescent rose; know it, and mark it with a mark. Then proceed from it along the mansions by the number of the days of the month that have elapsed, and you will know the mansion in which the crescent stands on that day. An example of this: we saw that the crescent rose on the first night in al-Sharaṭān, and seven days of the Arab month had passed. We wished to know the mansion in which the moon was on that day, so we counted seven mansions from al-Sharaṭān and came at last to al-Dhirāʿ; and so we knew that the moon was in al-Dhirāʿ. Reason by analogy upon that. And this is the form of the table. /fol. 14v./
[Fig. 9: the circular diagram (dāʾira) of the lunar mansions, as in the source — ]

The discourse on the mansion of al-Sharaṭān, and this is its figure: [star-figure of the mansion, as in the source]. To it belongs the letter (alif). When the moon descends into al-Sharaṭān — and it is fiery and inauspicious — there are valid in it such operations as pertain to the affairs of women. A spiritual force is stirred toward that, joined to the souls of kings; and in it there appear among them anger, violent seizure, and the shedding of blood. In this period the sages used to settle to sleep and to the absence of movement. Some of them have mentioned that a man sees in his sleep what strikes at him and troubles his temper, and that not sleeping at this time is preferable; and that one must hold to silence, speaking only of what is necessary or of what cannot be avoided.

Perform no craft in it. If you desire an operation, then perform in it operations of evil and corruption. Whoever is born in this mansion will be much given to corruption. Its suffumigation is pepper and black cumin. And God knows best.

The discourse on al-Buṭayn, and this is its figure: [star-figure of the mansion, as in the source]. To it belongs the letter (bāʾ). When the moon descends into al-Buṭayn — and it is hot and moist — there descends into the world /fol. 15r./ a wholesome, temperate spiritual force, fit for what pertains to the affairs of men rather than of women. In it talismans are set up; the operation of alchemy is valid in it, and every craft of exalted degree; and there are fit in it the commencement of the sciences, the casting of signet-rings, and engraving. Whoever is born in it lives happy, rightly guided, and beloved of created beings. Its suffumigation is aloeswood, saffron, and mastic.

The discourse on the mansion of al-Thurayyā, and this is its figure, and it is as you see: [star-figure of the mansion, as in the source]. To it belongs the letter (jīm). When the moon descends into al-Thurayyā — and it is a star of mixed substance — there descends into the world a spiritual force of mixed heat and cold. The making of talismans is fit in it; do in it what is fit for women, and the preparation of medicines efficacious against cold. Travellers fare well in it and gain abundant profit; and it is good in it to meet kings and to correspond with them. In it marriage is fit, and the purchase of slave-girls and of slaves; and whatever is undertaken in it is good, because it is the counterpart of the moon and not of the sun; and whatever is made in it is of praiseworthy outcome. Whoever is born in it will be fortunate: he detests debauchery, loves piety, and consorts with the righteous and the learned. Its suffumigation is linseed and black cumin. And God knows best.

The discourse on the mansion of al-Dabarān, and this is its figure: [star-figure of the mansion, as in the source]. To it belongs the letter (dāl). When the moon descends into al-Dabarān — and it is earthy — there descends into the world a spiritual force that works enmity, hatred, and corruption in the earth. So beware in it of striving after your needs and of beginning operations. Set up no talisman in it, and undertake no craft in it. In sum, all operations in it are of evil outcome. It is fit for nothing save the burying of the dead, the hoarding of wealth, the concealing of secrets, the digging of wells, and the cutting of river channels; it is fit for nothing besides that. Whoever is born in it will be blameworthy and forsaken. Its suffumigation is the rind of sweet pomegranate and male frankincense. And God knows best.

The discourse on the mansion of al-Haqʿa, and this is its figure: [star-figure of the mansion, as in the source]. To it belongs the letter (hāʾ). When the moon descends into al-Haqʿa — and it is mixed of inauspicious and auspicious — there descends into the earth a spiritual force that is at one time evil and at another mixed. So work in it at the violent workings of poisons and their compounds in particular. Undertake in it no craft of the sun and the moon; plant no crop in it; wear no garments in it, neither new nor worn; and do not marry in it, for all of that is of unpraiseworthy outcome. Stir not in it with anything of the operations of the spiritual beings. Whoever is born in it will be of praiseworthy outcome at the end of his life, but not at its beginning. Its suffumigation for that is nadd aloeswood, frankincense, benzoin (jāwī), and mastic.

The discourse on the mansion of al-Hanʿa, and this is its figure: [star-figure of the mansion, as in the source]. To it belongs the letter (wāw). When the moon descends into al-Hanʿa — and it is an auspicious star — then work in it the operations of inclining, /fol. 15v./ love, and affection; suffumigate in it with the incense; go in, in it, to kings and to the great ones; strive after their needs, and strive about their quarter; and in it join yourself to the noble among people and consort with the brethren. Begin in it the operations you desire; marry in it; buy in it slave-girls, slaves, and horses; plant trees in it; raise buildings in it; measure and weigh; travel in it; and sell and buy — all of that is of praiseworthy outcome. Whoever is born in it lives happy and dies a martyr. Its suffumigation is quṭrub and wormwood seed.

The discourse on the mansion of al-Dhirāʿ, and this is its figure: [star-figure of the mansion, as in the source]. To it belongs the letter (zāy). When the moon descends into al-Dhirāʿ — and it is airy, auspicious, and gentle — there descends into the world a wholesome spiritual force, fit for the handling of the spiritual beings, for the beginning of good works, for the suffumigations, and for assembling in houses of worship. In it talismans are set up, and in it are performed the operations of the nāranjiyyāt (nīranj-workings). In it one goes in to kings, and joins oneself to the noble among people and to the brethren. Whoever is born in it will be fortunate, rightly guided, and granted success. Its suffumigation is nettle seed and linseed.

The discourse on al-Nathra, and this is its figure: [star-figure of the mansion, as in the source]. To it belongs the letter (ḥāʾ). When the moon descends into al-Nathra — and it is cold mixed with heat, auspicious mixed with inauspicious — there descends into the world a spiritual force that works upon enmity, hatred, the severing of ties, and the like. It is fit for the making of the talismans that serve for that, and for invoking wrath upon enemies, transgressors, and the rancorous. In it the spiritual force of anger is stirred. So undertake in it no craft of the sun and the moon; do not go in to kings in it; and do not begin the making of the instruments of war, nor take counsel concerning them, for it is evil, and fit [only] for the operations of corruption, as we have mentioned. Whoever is born in it will be ill-starred. Its suffumigation is costus and pomegranate rind.

The discourse on the mansion of al-Ṭarf, and this is its figure: [star-figure of the mansion, as in the source]. To it belongs the letter (ṭāʾ). When the moon descends into al-Ṭarf — and it is a watery star, continuously inauspicious — there descends into the world a spiritual force that indicates the like of what has gone before, and its action is the stronger. So set up no talisman in it; undertake no craft in it; do not go in to kings in it; begin nothing of affection in it; and work no work of wisdom in it. Recite no adjuration. Solitude in it is better than mingling; and it is evil for all operations. Whoever is born in it will be ill-starred. Its suffumigation is nadd aloeswood and saffron.

The discourse on the mansion of al-Jabha, and this is its figure: [star-figure of the mansion, as in the source]. To it belongs (yāʾ). When the moon descends into al-Jabha — and it is cold, auspicious, mixed with inauspicious, and it is nearer to good than to corruption — in it one begins works of affection, and operations whose means lie near at hand, and going in to kings, and asking for what may be obtained through the fulfilment of needs. In it one is treated, and in it are treated slight ailments that are easily cured /fol. 16r./. In it removal from place to place, and travel, are fit; but the cutting out of new clothing and the wearing of it is disliked in it. Whoever is born in it will be adroit, fortunate, and granted success, though there is in him some guile and deceit. Its suffumigation is myrtle berries and saffron.

The discourse on the mansion of al-Kharthān, and this is its figure: [star-figure of the mansion, as in the source]. To it belongs the letter (kāf). When the moon descends into al-Kharthān — and it is al-Zubra — and it is hot and dry, it is fit for the handling of the spiritual beings, and for setting up talismans in it, and for the treatment of the sick and the curing of the chronically disabled, and for selling and buying, and for going in to kings and to chiefs. In it is fit the journey whose establishment one aims at, and residence; in it operations of exalted degree are fit; and in it the wearing of new clothing is fit. Whoever is born in it will be beloved among people, save that there is in him some guile, deceit, and dissimulation. Its suffumigation is the rind of sweet pomegranate, and nothing else. And God knows best.

The discourse on the mansion of al-Ṣarfa, and this is its figure: [star-figure of the mansion, as in the source]. To it belongs (lām). When the moon descends into al-Ṣarfa — and it is a star of mixed substance, of earth and fire — there descends into the world an auspicious spiritual force, fit for such operations as are middling. No craft is undertaken in it; the sick are not treated in it; and one does not go in to kings. But in it the instruments of war are made, in it arms are borne, and horses ridden. Whoever is born in it will be of evil disposition; he shuns people and people shun him — a schemer, a trickster, wicked, whom no one loves, by reason of the greatness of his evil and his guile. And God, exalted is He, knows best. Its suffumigation is nutmeg.

The discourse on the mansion of al-ʿAwwāʾ, and this is its figure: [star-figure of the mansion, as in the source]. To it belongs the letter (mīm). When the moon descends into al-ʿAwwāʾ — and it is a hot, dry star, auspicious mixed with inauspicious — there descends into the world a spiritual force that stirs up desire and engenders in men love for women and union with them. It is fit for the beginning of the teaching of knowledge and the teaching of everything. Do not undertake in it the craft of the noble stone, for it does not suit it. Do not make war upon enemies in it; let there be no quarrelling and no litigating; and do not go in to kings. It is fit that you wear new garments in it, and that garments be cut out in it. Whoever is born in it, male or female, will be a possessor of good fortune. The suffumigation for that is male frankincense. And God knows best.

The discourse on the mansion of al-Simāk, and this is its figure: [star-figure of the mansion, as in the source]. To it belongs the letter (nūn). When the moon descends into al-Simāk — and it is an earthy, dry star — there descends into the world a spiritual force that engenders enmity and the corruption of woman. It is fit for the making of deadly poisons and everything that engenders corruption. Beginning new and beneficial works is disliked, and selling, buying, and barter are disliked in it. Whoever is born in it will be a talebearer and a liar, of unpraiseworthy outcome. Its suffumigation is male frankincense and indigo seed.

The discourse on the mansion of al-Ghafr, and this is its figure: [star-figure of the mansion, as in the source] [editor's gloss (Old Spanish, fragmentary, standing in the figure area together with the numeral= 2): "…oble en ella quier cosa" — "…‑oble; in it, any thing"]. To it belongs the letter (sīn). When the moon descends into al-Ghafr — and it is an airy star there descends /fol. 16v./ during it into the world a spiritual force (rūḥāniyya) that produces love, affection, repose, and profit from kings. During it medicines are gathered, and those substances by which lethal poisons are dissolved and their harm repelled. During it the conducting of [the operation of] the noble stone is favourable; during it one works upon the spiritual beings; during it talismans are set up; and one may practise whatever accords with that among all the crafts and trades. Whoever is born under it will be ill-starred, possessed of cunning and deceit. And God knows best. Its suffumigation is male frankincense, and nothing else.

The discourse on the mansion of al-Zubānā, and this is its figure: [star-figure of the mansion, as in the source]. To it belongs the letter (ʿayn). When the moon descends into al-Zubānā — it is an airy star, auspicious but mixed with inauspiciousness — there descends during it into the world a spiritual force of a thing and its opposite; so operate during it in accordance with that. Whoever puts on a new garment [during it], a dog's bite will befall him, and enemies will speak evil words against him, and an ailment will fasten upon his body that pains him, and he will be hard put to be cured of it. Whoever is born under it will be fortunate in all his movements, whether male or female, though there is in him some cunning. And God knows best. Its suffumigation is wormwood seed and wild chamomile.

The discourse on the mansion of al-Iklīl, and this is its figure: [star-figure of the mansion, as in the source]. To it belongs the letter (fāʾ). When the moon descends into al-Iklīl — it is a star mixed of auspicious and inauspicious — there descends during it into the world a spiritual force that engenders enmity, hatred, and strife, and it works during it a thing and its opposite. Do not travel during it, do not marry, do not buy slaves, do not plant fruit-bearing trees or any others, and do not sow any crop: all of that is of unpraiseworthy outcome. Do not make up new garments during it, nor wear them; do not quarrel during it, nor go to law; and do not seek during it the fulfilment of needs. Whoever is born under it, whether male or female, will turn out base and ill-omened. Its suffumigation is pepper, saffron, and aloeswood.

The discourse on the mansion of al-Qalb, and this is its figure: [star-figure of the mansion, as in the source]. To it belongs the letter (ṣād). When the moon descends into al-Qalb — it is a fortunate star, watery and moist — there descends during it into the world a spiritual force that sets right what the preceding mansion has corrupted. It is favourable for buying weapons and the instruments of war, and for buying riding-beasts, and for farriery, and for uprooting trees, and for sowing and ploughing, and for bringing out what lies buried, and for treating livestock, and for drinking purgative medicines, and for bloodletting and cupping. Whoever is born under it will be ill-starred, whether male or female, though there is in him some cunning. And God knows best. Its suffumigation is myrobalan leaves.

The discourse on the mansion of al-Shawla, and this is its figure: [star-figure of the mansion, as in the source]. To it belongs the letter (qāf). When the moon descends into al-Shawla — it is an auspicious star turned aside by inauspiciousness — there descends during it into the world a mixed spiritual force that works during it a thing and its opposite. It is favourable for binding and loosing, and for such operations as are middling. But during it the cutting out of new clothing and the wearing of it are disapproved; do not set up a talisman during it, nor work upon the spiritual beings during it. Withdrawal from company during it is of praiseworthy outcome. Whoever is born under it, whether male or female, will be base, ill-omened, an inveterate liar, a talebearer, and depraved. Its suffumigation is pomegranate rind and mastic.

The discourse on the mansion of al-Naʿāʾim, and this is its figure: [star-figure of the mansion, as in the source]. To it belongs the letter (rāʾ). When the moon descends into al-Naʿāʾim, /fol. 17r./ it being fiery, fortunate, luminous, shining, and radiant, there descends during it into the world a spiritual force that purifies hearts and summons to affection, good fortune, and felicity; and it is of praiseworthy outcome in all circumstances. During it the conducting of the noble crafts is favourable; during it sayings of wisdom and the sciences of jurisprudence are recited; during it talismans are set up; during it building is built; and plant plantings during it, and wear new clothing during it, and cut out new clothing as well — for whoever wears new clothing will not cease to be in joy and gladness until that garment wears out. Whoever is born under it, whether male or female, will be granted success in all his movements and his restings. Its suffumigation is male frankincense and wormwood, and God knows best.

The discourse on the mansion of al-Balda, and this is its figure: [star-figure of the mansion, as in the source]. To it belongs the letter (shīn). When the moon descends into al-Balda — it is a fiery, inauspicious star — there descends during it into the world a spiritual force that works upon enmity, hatred, the severing of ties, and every evil; and nothing but that is to be done during it. So beware of setting up a talisman during it; do not conduct during it the operation of the noble stone or of the magnified gem; do not work upon the spiritual beings during it; do not sow any crop during it, nor set any planting; do not undertake any journey during it; and do not consort with kings during it. Whoever is born under it, whether male or female, will be ill-omened and a schemer. Its suffumigation is spikenard, aloeswood, and nadd, and God knows best.

The discourse on the mansion of Saʿd al-Dhābiḥ, and this is its figure: [star-figure of the mansion, as in the source]. To it belongs the letter (tāʾ). When the moon descends into Saʿd al-Dhābiḥ— it is an earthy star, inauspicious and mixed — there descends during it into the world a spiritual force that works during it hatred, enmity, and the severing of ties. The outcomes of affairs and of operations are not praiseworthy during it; during it the souls of kings are stirred to anger and wrath; and buying and selling are held blameworthy during it. Whoever is born under it, whether male or female, will be blessed, avid for this world, and a schemer after it. Its suffumigation is safflower.

The discourse on the mansion of Saʿd Bulaʿ, and this is its figure: [star-figure of the mansion, as in the source]. To it belongs the letter (thāʾ). When the moon descends into Saʿd Bulaʿ — it is a star mixed in substance, auspicious mixed with inauspicious — there descends during it into the world a spiritual force that works a thing and its opposite; it stands between the good and the bad. During it the buying of slaves and bondsmen is favourable, and it is suitable for buying riding-beasts, and for consorting with elders advanced in years, and for undertaking agricultural labours, and for cutting canals and digging wells, and for whatever of such works one may wish. It is suitable for excursions and outings, and for preparing foods and banquet-spreads. Whoever is born under it, whether male or female, will be blessed and righteous. Its suffumigation is chamomile.

The discourse on the mansion of Saʿd al-Suʿūd, and this is its figure: [star-figure of the mansion, as in the source]. To it belongs the letter (khāʾ). When the moon descends into Saʿd al-Suʿūd — it is a star mixed in substance, of earth and of air — there descends during it into the world /fol. 17v./ a spiritual force that effaces the traces of what came before it and is favourable for all operations. So begin during it with the operation of love and affection, and with whatever you wish of the acts that pertain to the mending of hearts. Work upon the spiritual beings during it, and set up talismans during it, and make contact during it with kings, chiefs, holders of office, and others; and do during it whatever you wish of the acts of affection — your operation will succeed. Whoever is born under it, whether male or female, will love the righteous. Its suffumigation is aloeswood and mastic, and God knows best.

The discourse on the mansion of Saʿd al-Akhbiya, and this is its figure: [star-figure of the mansion, as in the source]. To it belongs the letter (dhāl). When the moon descends into Saʿd al-Akhbiya — it is an airy, inauspicious star — there descends during it into the world a spiritual force that works during it the severing of ties, seditions, hatred, division, and wars. Operations are not brought to completion, and if they are completed their outcome is not praiseworthy. Do not treat the sick during it, nor undertake the treatments of spirits and of spiritual beings; do not set up talismans during it; and do not conduct during it the operation of alchemy (kīmiyāʾ) or of sīmiyāʾ. Whoever is born under it, whether male or female, will be depraved and an arrant unbeliever. Its suffumigation is male frankincense, sarcocolla (ʿanzarūt), and pepper.

The discourse on the mansion of al-Fargh al-Muqaddam, and this is its figure: [star-figure of the mansion, as in the source]. To it belongs the letter (ḍād). When the moon descends into al-Fargh al-Muqaddam — it is a watery, fortunate star — there descends during it into the world a spiritual force that works love during it, stirs up desire during it, and quickens souls with affection. During it the conducting of the alchemical operation is favourable, and the treatments of the spiritual beings, and the setting up of talismans, and the science of sīmiyāʾ. During it beneficial medicines are gathered; during it one may go in before kings and chiefs; and during it poisons are dissolved. Whoever is born under it will be of praiseworthy outcome. Its suffumigation is male frankincense, black cumin, and saffron. And God knows best, and that suffices.

The discourse on the mansion of al-Fargh al-Muʾakhkhar, and this is its figure: [star-figure of the mansion, as in the source]. To it belongs the letter (ẓāʾ). When the moon descends into al-Fargh al-Muʾakhkhar — it is a watery, fortunate star — there descends during it into the world a spiritual force that governs during it operations whose outcome is not praiseworthy, as was said above concerning the inauspicious mansions.

During it war is to be avoided, and the meeting of the enemy and of adversaries. During it kings shed blood; for this reason bloodletting and cupping are favourable during it, and likewise the performing of bleedings, and the binding of women and men from sexual intercourse. It is suitable for entering the bathhouse, and for removing the hair and the nails, and for drinking beneficial medicines. Whoever is born under it, whether male or female, will be ill-omened, depraved, full of guile, and treacherous. The suffumigation for that is pepper and cinnamon (dār ṣīnī).

The discourse on the mansion of al-Rishāʾ, and this is its figure: [star-figure of the mansion, as in the source]. To it belongs the letter (ghayn). When the moon descends into al-Rishāʾ — which is the Belly of the Fish, and it is watery and auspicious — there descends during it into the world a spiritual force of praiseworthy outcome; during it good operations and acts of good outcome are performed; and during it there is conducted /fol. 18r./ the craft of the noble stone and of the magnified, talismanically charged gem. Work upon the spiritual force during it. All operations during it are of praiseworthy outcome. It is suitable for travel, for marriage, for wearing new garments and cutting them out, and for moving from one place to another, and for consorting with sages and chiefs. Whoever is born under it will be blessed, whether male or female. Its suffumigation is black cumin, and God, exalted is He, knows best.
Faṣl: On the distribution of the mansions among the zodiacal signs, and the mansions belonging to each sign

Know that al-Muʾakhkhar, al-Rishāʾ, and one third of al-Sharaṭayn belong to the sign of Aries (al-Ḥamal); two thirds of al-Sharaṭayn, al-Buṭayn, and two thirds of al-Thurayyā belong to the sign of Taurus (al-Thawr); one third of al-Thurayyā, al-Dabarān, and al-Haqʿa belong to the sign of Gemini (al-Jawzāʾ); al-Hanʿa, al-Dhirāʿ, and one third of al-Nathra belong to the sign of Cancer (al-Saraṭān); one third of al-Nathra, al-Ṭarf, and two thirds of al-Jabha belong to the sign of Leo (al-Asad); one third of al-Jabha, al-Kharathān, and al-Ṣarfa belong to the sign of Virgo (al-Sunbula); al-ʿAwwāʾ, al-Simāk, and one third of al-Ghafr belong to the sign of Libra (al-Mīzān); two thirds of al-Ghafr, al-Zubānā, and two thirds of al-Iklīl belong to the sign of Scorpio (al-ʿAqrab); one third of al-Iklīl, al-Qalb, and al-Shawla belong to the sign of Sagittarius (al-Qaws); al-Naʿāʾim, al-Balda, and one third of al-Dhābiḥbelong to the sign of Capricorn (al-Jady); two thirds of al-Dhābiḥ, Bulaʿ, and two thirds of al-Suʿūd belong to the sign of Aquarius (al-Dalw); and one third of al-Suʿūd, al-Akhbiya, and al-Fargh al-Muqaddam belong to the sign of Pisces (al-Ḥūt).

Faṣl, in which I set out a table gathering the four seasons — spring, summer, autumn, and winter — and in which I also set out the twenty-eight mansions, the twelve zodiacal signs, and the Arab months; the exposition of that will come, if God, exalted is He, wills.

I say, concerning the figures of the mansions — and we have already made them plain in a manner other than this first one — that the first of them is al-Sharaṭayn: two stars set apart, one of them on the southern side and the other on the northern side, and they are the two horns of Aries; the brighter of the two is called al-Nāṭiḥ. To the eye's estimation, when they stand at mid-heaven the distance between them is about ten cubits. Near al-Simāk is a small star that sometimes goes before them. And this is the figure of al-Sharaṭayn: [Figure: star-diagram as in source — ]

As for al-Buṭayn, it is three small, dim stars forming an equilateral triangle, and they are the belly of Aries (al-Ḥamal). It was given a diminutive form only because Aries is many stars in the shape of a ram: al-Buṭayn is its belly, al-Thurayyā its fat tail, and al-Sharaṭayn its two horns. And the figure of al-Buṭayn is thus: [Figure: star-diagram as in source — ]

As for al-Thurayyā (the Pleiades), it is seven stars, six of them visible and one small and hidden, by which people test their eyesight. It was called /fol. 18v./ al-Thurayyā only from al-tharwa, which is abundance of dew and moisture. It has [several] names, among them al-Najm (the Star), even though in number they are stars. Some of the learned have said that what is intended by His words, exalted is He, By the star when it falls (Q 53:1) is al-Thurayyā, according to one of the opinions, and that the Arabs call al-Thurayyā a single "star" even though they are stars in number. The Messenger of God — God bless him and grant him peace — likewise called it "the Star", for he said, upon him be blessing and peace: ((When the Star rises, blight is lifted)) — meaning al-Thurayyā; and he meant [the lifting of blight] from the fruits. Among its names, too, are al-ʿUnqūd (the Cluster) and al-Qadam (the Foot) — so understand. And someone has recited these two verses:
When al-Thurayyā shows herself athwart the sky, he of the small eye sees her as seven stars, upon the midriff of the burning heaven, and she is as though a bracelet of pearl set upon a wrist.

And it is said that she wept because she could not overtake Suhayl (Canopus).

As for al-Nathra, it is two stars with the measure of a span between them, and in it is a smudge of whiteness like a scrap of cloud; and it is the nose of the lion. And this is its figure: [Figure: star-diagram as in source — ] And it is said that they are two stars. Some of them have said that the first of the Saʿds is Saʿd al-Suʿūd, then Saʿd al-Dhābiḥ, then Saʿd al-Akhbiya, then Saʿd Bulaʿ. The Saʿd stars are ten, four of them in the sign of Capricorn (al-Jady), in which the Moon lodges — and the four have been mentioned. As for the six that are not among the lunar mansions, they are Saʿd Nāshira, Saʿd al-Malik, Saʿd al-Bihām, Saʿd al-Humām, Saʿd al-Bāriʿ, and Saʿd Maṭar. Each Saʿd of these six has two stars, and between every two stars of them, to the eye, is the measure of a cubit; and they are ranged in sequence.

As for al-Fargh of the Bucket, the fore and the hind: each of the two is two stars, and between each star of them and the other are five cubits, as though the two were emptying out of the buckets. Al-Fargh al-Muʾakhkhar is the outlet of the water from the bucket, between the ʿarāqī (the cross-bars). And it is said that they are called al-Farghānī.

As for al-Rishāʾ, it is many small stars in the shape of a fish, called Baṭn al-Ḥūt (the belly of the Fish), and at its navel is a bright star in which the Moon lodges. /fol. 20r./ These, then, are the lunar mansions, which it traverses in every month. Each night the Moon is beside one of them, or near to it; then on the second night it passes on to the one after it, and is [beside] one of them or near to it. Between the rising of the sun and its setting there are 14 of them, and between its setting and its rising 14, and at the time of dawn two of the mansions. All of them rise from the east toward the west; and the time of their rising is to the left of one who is performing the prayer, and the time of their setting on his right, according to the differences of the climes. And the Sun likewise lodges in these mansions.

Know that the Arabs call the mansions al-anwāʾ. It is called nawʾ only because, when the setting one falls, then the rising one — that is, it heaves up (nahaḍa). And it is said that the nawʾ is the falling of one of the mansion-stars in the west at daybreak and the rising of its counterpart (raqīb) from the east, facing it at that very hour, every night, for 13 days; and so it is with every star until the term of the year is completed — save al-Jabha, for it has 14 days. I say: nowhere but in this passage has it been heard of the nawʾ that it means the falling. The Arabs used to attribute to them the rains, the winds, the cold, and the heat; and our master ʿUmar b. al-Khaṭṭāb — may God, exalted is He, be pleased with him — said: "We have been given rain by such-and-such a nawʾ."
Faṣl: On their risings

That is: the rising of al-Sharaṭayn falls when 19 nights of Nīsān (April) have elapsed, and on that day the Sun lodges in al-Iklīl. The rising of al-Buṭayn falls when one night of it remains. The rising of al-Thurayyā falls on the 13th of Ayyār (May); and it travels on for 50 nights after it has set at the west, then appears at daybreak from the east. When it stands at mid-heaven together with the setting of the sun, the cold grows severe and the blights are lifted from the fruits. And we have related that the Prophet — God bless him and grant him peace — said: ((When the Star rises, the blights are lifted.)) The rising of al-Dabarān falls on the 26th of Ayyār. The rising of al-Haqʿa falls when eight [nights] of Ḥazīrān (June) have elapsed. The rising of al-Hanʿa falls on the 21st of it. The rising of al-Dhirāʿ falls when four [nights] of Tammūz (July) have elapsed. The rising of al-Nathra falls when 17 nights of it have elapsed, together with the rising of al-Shiʿrā al-ʿAbūr. The rising of al-Ṭarf falls on the first night of Āb (August). The rising of al-Jabha falls when 14 nights of it have elapsed.

The rising of al-Zubra falls on the 29th of it. The rising of al-Ṣarfa falls when 8 [nights] of Aylūl (September) have elapsed. The rising of al-ʿAwwāʾ falls when 19 nights of it have elapsed. The rising of [al-Simāk] falls when 2 nights of it remain. The rising of [al-Ghafr] falls on the 12th of Tishrīn al-Awwal (October). The rising of [al-Zubānā] falls on the 25th of it. The rising of [al-Iklīl] falls on the 8th of Tishrīn al-Thānī (November). The rising of [al-Qalb] falls on the 21st of it. The rising of [al-Shawla] falls when 3 [nights] of Kānūn al-Awwal (December) have elapsed. The rising of [al-Naʿāʾim] falls when 16 nights of it have elapsed. The rising of [al-Balda] falls when 29 nights of it have elapsed. The rising of Saʿd al-Dhābiḥfalls when 11 nights of Kānūn al-Thānī (January) have elapsed. [The rising of Saʿd Bulaʿ] falls when 24 [nights] of it have elapsed. The rising of Saʿd [al-Suʿūd] /fol. 20v./ falls when 6 [nights] of Shubāṭ (February) have elapsed. The rising of Saʿd [al-Akhbiya] falls when 18 [nights] of it have elapsed. The rising of al-Fargh al-Muqaddam (the fore Fargh) falls when 2 nights of Ādhār (March) have elapsed. The rising of al-Fargh al-Muʾakhkhar (the hind
Fargh) falls when 14 nights of it have elapsed. The rising of al-Rishāʾ falls on the 4th of Nīsān (April).
Faṣl: On the division of these mansions among the four seasons

Know that to the season of spring belong al-Sharaṭayn, al-Buṭayn, al-Thurayyā, al-Dabarān, al-Haqʿa, al-Hanʿa, and al-Dhirāʿ; to the season of summer, al-Nathra, al-Ṭarf, al-Jabha, al-Zubra, al-Ṣarfa, al-Simāk, and al-ʿAwwāʾ; to the season of autumn, al-Ghafr, al-Zubānā, al-Iklīl, al-Qalb, al-Shawla, al-Naʿāʾim, and al-Balda; and to the season of winter, Saʿd al-Suʿūd, Saʿd al-Dhābiḥ, Saʿd al-Akhbiya, Saʿd Bulaʿ, the two Farghs — the fore and the hind — and al-Rishāʾ. And to each season belong seven mansions.
Faṣl: On the rhymed sayings (asjāʿ) of the Arabs relating to these mansions, and on what has been transmitted concerning them from the ancients

I read under our master Abū l-Yumn al-Kindī — may God, exalted is He, have mercy upon him — who said: I read under Abū Manṣūr al-Jawālīqī, who said: It reached me from Abū Bakr Muḥammad al-Marāwinī, who said: The Arabs say — when al-Sharaṭayn rises, the season is set aright, the boughs grow green, the homelands flourish, the neighbours exchange gifts, and the poor man passes the night in any place at all. When al-Buṭayn rises, the debt is discharged. When al-Thurayyā rises in the evening, [seek out] clothing for your herdsman; and if it rises in the morning, [seek out] for him a watering. When al-Dabarān rises, the ploughlands blaze and the pools dry up. When al-Haqʿa rises, the people turn back from the search for pasture. When al-Hanʿa rises, they betake themselves to the stronghold. When al-Dhirāʿ rises, the sun casts off her veil, the rays blaze up on the horizon, and the mirage shimmers over every low-lying plain. When al-Nathra rises, the bees yield in abundance, and there is not left in any milch beast a single drop. When al-Ṭarf rises, the matter of the guest becomes easy and light. When al-Jabha rises, the travellers set out in every direction. When al-Ṣarfa rises, every man of a craft plies his contrivance. When al-ʿAwwāʾ rises, the tent is pitched and the air grows sweet. When al-Simāk rises, the crowding (al-likāk) at the water grows great — that is to say, the press of the throng. When al-Ghafr rises, travel returns. When al-Zubānā rises, every man with a household takes up his own affair. When al-Iklīl rises, excuses avail nothing. When al-Qalb rises, every hardship is made light. When al-Shawla rises, the old man is hurried by the need to make water. When al-Naʿāʾim rises, the cold reaches every standing creature. When al-Balda rises, the [qishda] is eaten — and that is what comes out of the butter and the clarified fat at the bottom of the cooking pot; and in another transmission, al-jaʿda, which is a well-known plant. When Saʿd al-Suʿūd rises, the /fol. 21r./ wood grows green, the hides grow supple, and sitting in the sun becomes irksome. When al-Dhābiḥrises, the barker guards his people. When al-Akhbiya rises, people are urged to the wearing of the outer coats (aqbiya). When Saʿd Bulaʿ rises, the spring foal presses forward — that is, it grows strong enough for walking — and there comes to be upon the earth a glistening, that is, the herbage is sown. When al-Fargh al-Muqaddam rises, then serve, and you shall not regret it. When al-Fargh al-Muʾakhkhar rises, then make haste, and do not lag behind. When al-Samaka rises, movement becomes possible and the burr (al-ḥasaka) clings — that is, the burr of the saʿdān plant. These, then, are the rhymed sayings of the Arabs; we have mentioned a portion of them for the sake of the need [there is for them]. And God knows best.
How to Know Which Sign the Moon Is In
Manbaʿ Uṣūl al-Ḥikma, vol. I, p. 29

To know which sign the Moon is in: take the day of the Arabic month, multiply it by two, and add five to it. Then, starting from the sign the Sun occupies that day, count off five for each sign in turn, [I 30] continuing until the number in hand is used up. Whichever sign the count ends on, the Moon is in that sign that day and that night.

For example: on the eighth day of August, which is the twentieth day of the Arabic month of Safer, the Sun is in Leo, the fifth sign. We multiply twenty by two, giving forty. We add five to that, giving forty-five. Then, starting from Leo, the fifth sign, we count off five for each sign in turn.
This count ends on Aries. So the Moon is in Aries that day and that night.

How to Know Which Sign the Moon Is In If you want to know, from the table below, which sign the Moon is in: place your index finger on the section showing the days of the Arabic month, then place your thumb on whichever Gregorian month you are in. Then point with both fingers to where they meet on the table's grid. The sign written in that cell is the sign the Moon is in at that moment.

For example: we are in the Gregorian month of November and the twenty-fifth (25) day of the Arabic month. On the table, moving right to left, we find the month of November. Moving from top to bottom, we find the twenty-fifth (25), which marks the day of the Arabic month. Looking at where these two cells meet, we see that the cell contains Virgo (Sunbule). So the Moon is in Virgo that day and that night.

Let us give one more example, so that this is properly understood. We are in the Gregorian month of January and the twenty-eighth (28) day of the Arabic month. After finding the month of January on the table, we find the day of the Arabic month running from top to bottom — we find the twenty-eighth (28). Looking at where these two cells meet, we see that the cell contains Sagittarius (Kavs). The Moon is in Sagittarius that day and that night.

Let us give still one more example, for the ease of those who seek this science. We are in the Gregorian month of March and the 27th day of the Arabic month. Having found March, and having found the 27th of the Arabic month, we look at where these two cells meet and see Aquarius (Deliv). So the Moon is in Aquarius that day and that night.

[I 34] The Mansions of the Sun The Sun's mansions consist of the twelve (12) zodiac signs, and the Sun remains in each of them for one month.
The Sun remains in Aries (Hamel) between March 21 and April 20. The element of Aries is fire.
The Sun remains in Taurus (Sevr) between April 21 and May 21. The element of Taurus is earth.
The Sun remains in Gemini (Cevza) between May 22 and June 21. The element of Gemini is air.
The Sun remains in Cancer (Seretan) between June 22 and July 23. The nature of Cancer is water.
The Sun remains in Leo (Esed) between July 24 and August 23. The nature of Leo is fire.
The Sun remains in Virgo (Sunbule) between August 24 and September 23. The element of Virgo is earth.
The Sun remains in Libra (Mīzān) between September 24 and October 23. The element of Libra is air.
The Sun remains in Scorpio (Akrep) between October 24 and November 22. The element of Scorpio is water.
The Sun remains in Sagittarius (Kavs) between November 23 and December 21. The element of Sagittarius is fire.
The Sun remains in Capricorn (Cedi) between December 22 and January 20. The element of Capricorn is earth.
The Sun remains in Aquarius (Deliv) between January 21 and February 19. The element of Aquarius is air.
The Sun remains in Pisces (Hut) between February 20 and March 20. The element of Pisces is water. The Sun's course continues onward in this same order.
